clue.text: Apt, possibly, to present Fred and Ginger's speciality

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says three letters doing a dance, i.e. jumbled, and one such jumble of those letters is the clue's word Apt

explanation.surface: A dancing act fit to show off what Astaire and Rogers did best.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split as TAP + DANCING, is an instruction to rearrange TAP, and the result could be APT. 'to present' links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers were the famous Hollywood partnership known for their footwork routines on screen.

clue.text: Eurasian offering Sunday's roast with 33 per cent off

indicators.note: off means removed, so part of the roast's name is taken away

parts.note: turkey is the roast on the Sunday this puzzle anticipates, Christmas Day
a third of a six-letter word is two letters, here its final pair

explanation.surface: A shop offering a Sunday roast at a third off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 33 per cent off' removes two of six letters, EY. A Turk is Eurasian because Turkey spans Europe and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey straddles Europe and Asia, so one of its people can fairly be called Eurasian.

clue.text: Opted to get round my boss!

parts.note: to plump is to swell, become round
ED, the editor, is the crossword setter's boss

explanation.surface: A worker chooses flattery to win over their manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get round' looks like persuading; it means becoming plump. The setter's boss is the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for something is an idiom meaning to choose it after some hesitation.

clue.text: For instance, James Stewart fantasy 'It's a Wonderful Life'

parts.note: the actor Jimmy Stewart is an example of an American
a fantasy is a dream

explanation.surface: James Stewart's best-loved film, the Christmas classic, imagined as a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title stands for the ideal it shows: an ordinary American's hopes for a good life in his small town.
explanation.definitionFit: The idea that any citizen of the USA can prosper and live well is summed up by a Christmas film's title.

clue.text: Bike to bridge in the morning going down to new plant

indicators.note: in a down entry, going down to means the first piece comes above, before, the next
to bridge is to span a gap, so the word for bike goes over and around the morning letters

parts.note: to bike is to cycle
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: Cycling across a bridge at dawn on the way to a new plant nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bridge' has the bike word span the morning letters, and in a down entry 'going down to' means the new letter follows below.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamen is a flowering species with swept-back petals, popular as a winter pot plant.

clue.text: Wound up in big city catching Queen on Five

indicators.note: catching means trapping, so the other letters are held within the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY, New York, is the Big Apple

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A tense viewer in New York sees the Queen on Channel Five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' holds the monarch over the numeral inside the city. Channel 5 is a British TV channel, hence 'Five'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge, tense and jittery, is to be keyed up, a state described as anxious.

clue.text: Tiny mite that delivers half the letters

definitions.meaning: the smallest particle, a tiny bit of anything
A to M covers the first half of the 26-letter alphabet

explanation.surface: A minuscule creature that somehow carries half the post.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A TO M: the letters from A to M are thirteen of the twenty-six, half the alphabet. 'Mite' is a tiny amount, not the bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a tiny amount, and the smallest particle of matter is the classic example of tininess.

clue.text: Upcoming Test pitch needs rolling before a fair game

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means rising, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for cars

indicators.note: rolling over turns something round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to pitch, throw high

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch needs rolling before the next Test, ahead of a fair game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' reverses MOT and 'needs rolling' reverses LOB. The surface is cricket; the MOT is Britain's yearly car safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: Tombola is a raffle with prizes drawn from a revolving drum, a staple of fêtes and fairs.

clue.text: Lovers seeing film, 'Hair', sharing time

parts.note: a mist is a thin film of moisture

indicators.note: sharing says the two words overlap on one letter, so it appears only once

parts.note: tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Lovers go to see the musical Hair together.
explanation.walkthrough: MIST ends with T and TRESSES begins with it; 'sharing time' means the one T serves both.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress is a woman in an extramarital affair, so the plural are illicit partners.

clue.text: 14, wearing this?!

parts.note: the clue refers to the answer of 14 across, a word for embarrassed: a face looks that way if it has this cosmetic on

explanation.surface: Someone looking flushed, perhaps because of their make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 across is RED-FACED; a red face may be blushing or simply wearing red make-up. The word is also French for red.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is the reddish cosmetic powder put on the cheeks, which would make anyone look flushed.

clue.text: Seasonal event with sadly miscast entertaining personnel

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting a guest, so one piece holds the other inside it
sadly says the casting went wrong, so the letters of miscast are rearranged

parts.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A festive show spoiled because the actors were badly chosen, nativity-play style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges the word miscast into CISTMAS, and 'entertaining' has that host the personnel letters after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival of 25 December comes round every winter, the main event of the holiday season.

clue.text: Lack of sense caused by a fall?

definitions.text: Lack of sense caused by a fall?

parts.words: Lack of sense caused by a fall?
parts.note: the fall is a fall of flakes from the sky, and the sense lost is sight, dazzled by the glare

explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests a tumble and 'Lack of sense' foolishness; really it is a snowfall that takes away vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare from a white landscape can temporarily damage the eyes, robbing a person of their sight.

clue.text: Page with scripture passage: Our Lady's clothed in blue maybe

indicators.note: clothed in says this name is wrapped in the other pieces, as if dressed in them

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is the school scripture lesson
a col is a pass between mountains, a way through
taken as written
Our Lady is the Virgin Mary, and the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A page of Bible reading about the Virgin Mary in her traditional blue robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothed in' wraps the other pieces round Our Lady's name. 'Our' does double duty on the surface but supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is one of the three basic hues, with red and yellow, from which painters mix the others.

clue.text: Perhaps drawing used by copper delayed arresting the writer, say

indicators.note: arresting means seizing and holding, so these pieces close around the setter's letter

parts.note: drawing is one example of art
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the writer is the setter, who refers to themself as I
something delayed is late

explanation.surface: A police officer, slow to act, takes the sketch artist into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' has the drawing and the metal close round the writer's letter. 'copper' is a police officer on the surface, the metal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to put into words, express clearly, which is what saying something does.

clue.text: Embarrassed being 12 and overlooked

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, a primary colour, here red
a building that overlooks something faces it, so overlooked means faced

explanation.surface: Feeling embarrassed at having been passed over.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' points to PRIMARY COLOUR, of which red is an example. 'overlooked' looks like 'ignored' but means 'looked out on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is ashamed blushes, so a flushed face is the outward sign of embarrassment.

clue.text: Oscar cuts tubas for broadcast — they'll be hidden under the surface

definitions.text: they'll be hidden under the surface

indicators.note: cuts in the sense of cutting into, so one letter goes into the word tubas
broadcast as in seeds scattered widely, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winning soundtrack chops tuba parts for a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for broadcast' rearranges TUBAS to UBATS, and 'cuts' slips O into it. 'broadcast' tempts a sound-alike reading; here it means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: German submarines of the World Wars travelled submerged, lurking beneath the waves to attack shipping.

clue.text: Admires northbound lasses in oilskin coats

indicators.note: northbound in a down entry means going upwards, so the letters are read in reverse
coats as a verb, covering, so the answer sits wrapped within these words

explanation.surface: Girls heading north in waterproofs, much admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' covers SESINOIL in 'lasSES IN OILskin', and 'northbound' turns it round. 'coats' looks like clothing beside 'oilskin'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, which is admiring them greatly.

clue.text: Heart shown by popular bank

parts.note: something popular is in, in fashion
a bank of a river is one of its sides

explanation.surface: A loved bank with plenty of heart, as its adverts would claim.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its central part, the bit within, away from the edges.

clue.text: Knocked back seconds with syrup on top

parts.note: syrup is Cockney rhyming slang for a wig (syrup of figs), so wearing one on top is being wigged

explanation.surface: Someone downs a second helping with syrup poured over it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang uses 'syrup of figs' for 'wig', shortened to 'syrup'.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock back a drink is an idiom for gulping it down in one, a hearty mouthful.

clue.text: Sue flipped price tag — it illustrates trousers

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the concealed letters are read from right to left
trousers as a verb, pocketing something, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Someone angrily turns over a price label that shows a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' pockets ETAGITIL in 'pricE TAG IT ILlustrates', and 'flipped' turns it round. Both indicators look like part of a shopping scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to bring a lawsuit against them, taking the dispute to court.

clue.text: Bullets turned in, plus a chemical used in explosives

parts.note: ammo, ammunition, is bullets

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so this short word reads backwards

explanation.surface: Bullets handed in along with an ingredient for bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses IN. 'plus' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is a pungent nitrogen compound whose derivatives, like ammonium nitrate, make blasting agents.

clue.text: Country briefly capturing the heart of its ruler's father and son

definitions.text: Country briefly capturing the heart of its ruler's father and son

parts.words: Country briefly capturing the heart of its ruler's father and son
parts.note: the nation's short form is two letters, and those two are the middle of the title held by the king's father and by his sons

explanation.surface: A nation fond of the royal line of fathers and sons.
explanation.walkthrough: The country's abbreviation UK is the heart of DUKE: King Charles's father Philip was Duke of Edinburgh, and his sons are Dukes of Cornwall and Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's full official name covers England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland under one monarch.

clue.text: Clue: 'A welcoming northern country'

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a key is a clue to solving something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword clue presented as a quotation about a friendly northern land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' takes the northern letter in. The quotation marks make the clue look like a puzzle within a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is an East African nation on the equator, bordering Tanzania and Ethiopia.

clue.text: Facility that's furnished for 10

definitions.meaning: a facility is a natural talent or knack
10 across is Christmas, when presents are given out

explanation.definitionFit: A natural flair is a talent, and a Christmas present is something handed over at the season.

clue.text: What often follows Yuletide games? Unfortunately, anger must!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A family warning that board games at Christmas always end in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges ANGER MUST. The surface makes the anagram fodder look like a grim prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: Disputes and quarrels are what families notoriously fall into after competitive festive board games.

clue.text: In retirement, occasionally encountered piquant Noel lassitude

indicators.note: retirement as going back, so the chosen letters are read from right to left
occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A retired person chances upon a spicy Christmas carol and feels listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters IUNNE from 'piquant Noel', and 'In retirement' turns them round. 'encountered' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, the weary lack of energy that lassitude describes.

clue.text: Stops tips

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb, brings to a stop
tips as a noun, the extremities of things

explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to halt it, and the tips of an object are its extremities.

clue.text: Synthetic tree decoration with timer at first going too quickly

parts.note: synthetic means artificial, false
a star is often fixed to the top of a Christmas tree

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of the word timer is wanted

explanation.surface: An artificial Christmas tree topped with a decoration on a timer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes T from 'timer'. The festive surface hides a running race.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race, a runner who moves before the gun commits this foul by leaving too early.
